file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 (`nvidia-a6000`) |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (Focal) |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM) – you can change this to suit your workload |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (pick any zone that supports GPUs) |
| **Project** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` – replace with your actual GCP project ID |
| **Billing** | Must be enabled for the project |
| **API** | Uses the **gcloud CLI** (recommended) and the **REST API** (curl) |

> **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the term “EC2”; that’s AWS terminology.  
> * The GPU type `nvidia-a6000` is only available in certain zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).  
> * You must enable the **Compute Engine API** and the **GPU API** (`compute.googleapis.com`) in your project.  
> * Ensure you have the **`roles/compute.admin`** role (or equivalent) on the project.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID

# 2️⃣  Choose a zone that supports GPUs
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--boot-disk-type=pd-ssd` | SSD persistent disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional startup script (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers) |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules |
| `--scopes` | OAuth scopes (full cloud platform access) |

> **Tip:** If you need more than one GPU, change `count=1` to the desired number (max 8 per instance).

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

Below is a **JSON payload** you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace placeholders (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, `YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME`) with your values.

```bash
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Authenticate (you can use gcloud auth application-default login)
gcloud auth application-default login

# Get an access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances"
```

### Notes on the REST payload

- **`machineType`** – fully qualified path to the machine type.  
- **`guestAccelerators`** – attaches the GPU.  
- **`disks.initializeParams.sourceImage`** – points to the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.  
- **`metadata.startup-script`** – optional; installs NVIDIA drivers automatically.  
- **`serviceAccounts`** – grants the instance full cloud‑platform access.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API & GPU API |
| ✅ | Billing enabled for the project |
| ✅ | Project has `roles/compute.admin` (or equivalent) |
| ✅ | Choose a GPU‑capable zone (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.) |
| ✅ | Use `nvidia-a6000` accelerator type |
| ✅ | Install NVIDIA drivers (via startup script or manually) |
| ✅ | Adjust machine type / GPU count as needed |

---

### Example Startup Script (`startup.sh`)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
sudo apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (replace 535 with the latest supported version)
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to load the driver (optional)
# sudo reboot
```

> Save this script locally and reference it with `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` in the gcloud command.

---

## 4. Verify the Instance

After creation, you can check the instance status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a
```

Look for:

- `status: RUNNING`
- `guestAccelerators` showing `nvidia-a6000`
- `disks` showing the SSD boot disk

You can SSH into the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a
```

Once inside, verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Wrap‑Up

- **gcloud** is the simplest way to spin up a GPU instance.  
- **REST API** gives you programmatic control (useful for CI/CD pipelines).  
- Always double‑check the zone and GPU availability.  
- Remember to clean up resources when done to avoid unnecessary charges.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
